outcomes.text: State the distinguishing properties of solids, liquids and gases.
Describe the particle separation, arrangement and motion in each state.
Explain changes of state using kinetic particle theory.
Interpret heating and cooling curves using kinetic particle theory.
Explain how temperature and pressure affect gas volume using kinetic theory.
Describe and explain diffusion using kinetic particle theory.
Explain how relative molecular mass affects the rate of diffusion of gases.
Describe how elements, compounds and mixtures differ.

topics.title: 2.2 Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

subtopics.title: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

outcomes.text: Describe the atom as a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons in shells.
State the relative charges and masses of protons, neutrons and electrons.
Define proton (atomic) number.
Define mass (nucleon) number.
Work out electronic configurations of atoms and ions with proton number 1 to 20.
Link outer electrons to group number, shells to period number, and noble gases to full outer shells.
Define isotopes.
Explain why isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties.
Interpret and use symbols for atoms and ions.
Calculate relative atomic mass from isotope masses and abundances.
Describe the formation of cations and anions.
Describe the giant lattice structure of ionic compounds.
State that an ionic bond is a strong electrostatic attraction between opposite ions.
Describe how ionic bonds form between metals and non-metals, using dot-and-cross diagrams.
Explain the high melting and boiling points of ionic compounds.
Explain their electrical conductivity when molten or aqueous but not solid.
State that a covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons giving noble gas configurations.
Describe covalent bonding in simple molecules, using dot-and-cross diagrams.
Explain the low melting and boiling points of simple molecular compounds.
Explain their poor electrical conductivity.
Describe the giant covalent structures of graphite, diamond and silicon(IV) oxide.
Relate the structures of graphite and diamond to their uses.
Describe the similar properties of diamond and silicon(IV) oxide in terms of structure.
Describe metallic bonding as attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons.
Explain the electrical conductivity of metals.
Explain malleability and ductility of metals.
State the formulae of the elements and compounds named in the content.
Define molecular formula.
Define empirical formula.
Deduce a compound's formula from a model or diagram.
Deduce the formula of an ionic compound from ion charges.
Write word, symbol and ionic equations with state symbols.
Deduce a symbol equation with state symbols from given information.

topics.title: 3.2 Relative masses of atoms and molecules

subtopics.title: Relative masses of atoms and molecules

outcomes.text: Describe relative atomic mass, Ar.
Define relative molecular mass and relative formula mass, Mr.

topics.title: 3.3 The mole and the Avogadro constant

subtopics.title: The mole and the Avogadro constant

outcomes.text: State what a mole is and the value of the Avogadro constant.
Use amount = mass / molar mass in calculations of amount, mass, molar mass, relative mass and particle numbers.
Use the molar gas volume of 24 dm3 at r.t.p.
State that concentration is measured in g/dm3 or mol/dm3.
Calculate reacting masses, limiting reactants, gas volumes and solution concentrations and volumes.
Calculate a solution's concentration from titration data.
Calculate empirical and molecular formulae from data.
Calculate percentage yield, percentage composition and percentage purity.
Define electrolysis.
Identify the anode, cathode and electrolyte.
Describe the transfer of charge: electron movement, electron loss and gain, and ion movement.
Identify products and observations for molten lead(II) bromide, concentrated aqueous sodium chloride and dilute sulfuric acid.
Identify products when electrolysing aqueous copper(II) sulfate with carbon and copper electrodes.
State that metals or hydrogen form at the cathode and non-metals at the anode.
Predict products for molten binary compounds.
Predict products for halide solutions, dilute or concentrated.
Write ionic half-equations for oxidation at the anode and reduction at the cathode.
State why metal objects are electroplated.
Describe how metals are electroplated.
State that a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell makes electricity with water as the only product.
Compare fuel cells with petrol engines in vehicles.
State that exothermic reactions give out thermal energy and warm the surroundings.
State that endothermic reactions take in thermal energy and cool the surroundings.
State that the energy transfer is the enthalpy change, with its sign for each type.
Define activation energy.
Draw, label and interpret reaction pathway diagrams.
Explain enthalpy change using bond breaking and bond making.
Calculate enthalpy change using bond energies.
Identify physical and chemical changes and describe how they differ.
Describe collision theory in terms of particle concentration, collision frequency, kinetic energy and activation energy.
State how a catalyst affects rate and activation energy.
Explain the effects of concentration, pressure, surface area, temperature and catalysts, including enzymes, on rate.
Describe and evaluate practical methods for investigating rate.
Interpret rate-of-reaction data and graphs.
State that some reactions are reversible.
Describe changing the direction of reversible reactions for hydrated and anhydrous compounds.
State the two conditions for equilibrium in a closed system.
Predict how temperature, pressure, concentration and a catalyst affect the equilibrium position.
State the Haber process equation and the sources of its reactants.
State the typical conditions of the Haber process.
State the Contact process equation and the sources of its reactants.
State the typical conditions of the Contact process.
Explain the conditions used in both processes in terms of rate, equilibrium, safety and economics.
Use Roman numerals for oxidation numbers.
Define redox as simultaneous reduction and oxidation.
Define oxidation by oxygen, electrons and oxidation number.
Define reduction by oxygen, electrons and oxidation number.
Identify redox by oxygen or electron transfer.
Identify redox by changes in oxidation number using the rules.
Identify redox by colour changes with potassium manganate(VII) or potassium iodide.
Define oxidising and reducing agents.
Identify oxidation, reduction and agents in reactions.

topics.title: 7.1 The characteristic properties of acids and bases

outcomes.text: State that acids contain H+ ions and alkalis contain OH- ions in solution.
Define acids as proton donors and bases as proton acceptors.
State that bases are metal oxides or hydroxides and alkalis are soluble bases.
Describe acid reactions with metals, bases and carbonates.
Describe base reactions with acids and ammonium salts.
State that neutralisation occurs between an acid and a base.
Describe the acid-alkali neutralisation ionic equation.
Describe the effect of acids and alkalis on litmus, thymolphthalein and methyl orange.
Define strong and weak acids by dissociation.
Give examples of strong acids and write their dissociation equations.
Give examples of weak acids and write their partial dissociation equations.
Compare acidity using pH and universal indicator.
Describe amphoteric oxides.
Classify oxides as acidic, basic or amphoteric.
Describe preparing soluble salts from an acid with an alkali, metal, insoluble base or insoluble carbonate.
Describe preparing insoluble salts by precipitation.
Describe the general solubility rules for salts.
Define hydrated and anhydrous substances.
Define water of crystallisation.
Describe the Periodic Table as periods and groups in order of proton number.
Describe the change from metallic to non-metallic character across a period.
Relate group number to the charge of ions formed.
Explain similar properties within a group using electronic configuration.
Use an element's position to predict its properties.
Identify trends in groups from given information.
Describe lithium, sodium and potassium and their trends down the group.
Predict properties of other Group I elements.
Describe chlorine, bromine and iodine and their trends down the group.
State the appearance of the halogens at r.t.p.
Explain halogen displacement reactions with halide ions.
Predict properties of other Group VII elements.
Describe transition elements as dense, high-melting metals with variable oxidation numbers, coloured compounds and catalytic activity.
Describe noble gases as unreactive monatomic gases and explain this using electronic configuration.
Compare physical properties of metals and non-metals.
Describe reactions of metals with dilute acids, cold water and steam, and oxygen.
Describe uses of metals in terms of physical properties, such as aluminium in aircraft, cables and food containers and copper in wiring.
Describe alloys as mixtures of a metal with other elements, including brass and stainless steel.
Explain why alloys are harder and stronger than pure metals.
Describe alloy uses in terms of properties.
Identify alloys from structure diagrams.
State the order of the reactivity series.
Describe relative reactivity using displacement reactions.
Describe metal reactions with cold water, steam and dilute hydrochloric acid and explain them using the series.
Explain the apparent unreactivity of aluminium.
Deduce an order of reactivity from experimental results.
State the conditions needed for rusting.
Describe how barrier methods prevent rusting.
State common barrier methods.
Explain sacrificial protection.
Describe galvanising as barrier and sacrificial protection.
Describe how a metal's reactivity relates to ease of extraction.
Describe iron extraction in the blast furnace with the equation for each step.
Describe aluminium extraction, including cryolite, replacing anodes and electrode reactions.
Describe chemical tests for water.
Describe testing water purity using melting and boiling points.
Explain why distilled water is used in practical work.
State substances that natural water may contain.
State which of these substances are beneficial.
State which are potentially harmful.
Describe the treatment of domestic water supply.
State that ammonium salts and nitrates are fertilisers.
Describe NPK fertilisers and why they improve plant growth.
State the composition of clean, dry air.
State the source of each major air pollutant.
State the adverse effects of each pollutant.
Describe how carbon dioxide and methane cause global warming.
State and explain strategies to reduce climate change and acid rain.
Explain how nitrogen oxides form in engines and how catalytic converters remove them.
Describe photosynthesis.
State the word and symbol equations for photosynthesis.
State what a structural formula is.
Draw and interpret displayed formulae.
Write and interpret general formulae of alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids.
Define structural isomers.
Identify a functional group.
Describe the characteristics of a homologous series.
State what a saturated compound is.
State what an unsaturated compound is.
Name and draw unbranched alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and reaction products with up to four carbons.
State the compound type from a name ending or a formula.
Name and draw unbranched esters from alcohols and acids with up to four carbons.
Name the fossil fuels.
Name methane as the main constituent of natural gas.
State what hydrocarbons are.
State that petroleum is a mixture of hydrocarbons.
Describe separating petroleum by fractional distillation.
Describe how fraction properties change up the column.
Name the uses of each petroleum fraction.
State that alkanes have single covalent bonds and are saturated hydrocarbons.
Describe alkanes as generally unreactive except for combustion and chlorine substitution.
State what a substitution reaction is.
Describe photochemical substitution of alkanes with chlorine and draw the products.
State that alkenes have a carbon double bond and are unsaturated.
Describe making alkenes and hydrogen by cracking.
Describe the reasons for cracking.
Describe the bromine test for unsaturation.
State what an addition reaction is.
Describe alkene addition with bromine, hydrogen and steam, and draw the products.
Describe making ethanol by fermentation and by steam addition to ethene, comparing the methods.
Describe the combustion of alcohols.
State the uses of ethanol as a solvent and fuel.
Describe reactions of carboxylic acids with metals, bases and carbonates, naming the salts.
Describe forming ethanoic acid by oxidising ethanol.
Describe forming an ester from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.
Define polymers and monomers.
Identify repeat units and linkages in addition and condensation polymers.
Deduce addition polymer structures from alkenes and the reverse.
Deduce condensation polymer structures: polyamides and polyesters.
Describe the differences between addition and condensation polymerisation.
State that plastics are made from polymers.
Describe how plastic properties affect disposal.
Describe the environmental challenges of plastics.
Describe and draw nylon and PET.
State that PET can be recycled to monomers.
Describe proteins as natural polyamides made of amino acids.
Describe and draw the structure of proteins.
Name apparatus for measuring time, temperature, mass and volume.
Suggest advantages and disadvantages of methods and apparatus.
Describe solvent, solute, solution, saturated solution, residue and filtrate.
Describe an acid-base titration using a burette, pipette and indicator.
Describe how to identify the end-point with an indicator.
Describe how paper chromatography separates soluble mixtures.
Describe locating agents for colourless substances.
Interpret chromatograms to identify unknowns and pure or impure substances.
State and use the Rf equation.
Describe and explain separation using a solvent, filtration, crystallisation, simple and fractional distillation.
Suggest suitable techniques for given substances.
Identify substances and assess purity using melting and boiling points.
Describe tests for the anions carbonate, halides, nitrate, sulfate and sulfite.
Describe tests for cations using sodium hydroxide and ammonia.
Describe tests for ammonia, carbon dioxide, chlorine, hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur dioxide.
Describe flame tests for lithium, sodium, potassium, calcium, barium and copper(II).
